cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, and his brother Aaron, the priest. This time the subject is the human body. Buckle up, friend, because Leviticus does NOT do small talk.

cards.question: Who are Moses and Aaron supposed to pass this message on to?

cards.text: Here's the first case. When any man has a bodily discharge, the discharge is unclean.

cards.question: When a man has a bodily discharge, where does his uncleanness come from?

cards.text: Flowing or blocked, his discharge brings about uncleanness. And it doesn't stay with him: any bed he lies on and any furniture he sits on becomes unclean too.

cards.question: Someone touches the bed of the man with the discharge. What must that person do?

answers.text: Wash his clothes and bathe with water
Shave off all his hair and his beard
Stay outside the camp for a whole week

cards.question: Someone sits on furniture where the man with the discharge was sitting. True or false: that person must wash and bathe too.

cards.text: Touch his body, or get spit on by him, and it's wash, bathe, unclean until evening. Friend, in that camp your clothes got washed MORE than they got worn.

cards.question: True or false: a saddle the man with the discharge rides on stays clean.

cards.text: Whoever touches anything that was under him is unclean until evening. Whoever carries those things has to wash and bathe as well.

cards.question: The man with the discharge touches someone. When does that person have to wash and bathe?

answers.text: When he didn't rinse his hands first
When he touched them after dark
When he touched them on the Sabbath

cards.text: Now the law walks right into the kitchen. And friend, as a kitchen tool myself, I am holding my BREATH.

cards.question: Any clay pot the man with the discharge touches must be ___.
True or false: a wooden utensil the man with the discharge touches must be broken too.

cards.text: Then the good news: the man is cleansed from his discharge, and he counts off seven days. Believe me, I counted the dust in a junk drawer for YEARS.

cards.question: After counting off his seven days, the cleansed man washes his clothes. What does he bathe himself in?

cards.text: On the eighth day, he comes before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, bringing two birds.

cards.question: On the eighth day, who does the cleansed man give his two birds to?
The priest sacrifices the man's two birds. What are they offered as?

answers.text: A sin offering and a burnt offering
A guilt offering and a grain offering
A peace offering and a wave offering

cards.text: In this way the priest makes atonement for the man before the LORD because of his discharge. He isn't left stuck, friend: the way through is written right there.
Next comes a shorter case. When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water.

cards.question: True or false: after an emission of semen, the man brings two birds to the priest on the eighth day.

cards.text: Any clothing or leather with semen on it gets washed with water and stays unclean until evening. Then the law covers a man and a woman together.

cards.question: True or false: if a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, only the man has to bathe.

cards.text: Now the law turns to women. When a woman has her flow of blood, she is unclean due to her menstruation.

cards.question: A woman is unclean due to her menstruation for ___ days.
During a woman's period, what happens to anyone who touches her?

answers.text: They bring two birds to the priest

cards.text: Anything she lies or sits on during her period is unclean. Touch her bed or her furniture, and the laundry's back: wash, bathe, unclean until evening.
Then a man lies with her during her period, and her flow touches him. Friend, that is a LOT closer than bumping into her furniture.

cards.question: True or false: if a man lies with a woman during her period and her flow touches him, he is unclean only until evening.

cards.text: Then a different case. A woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside her period, or it keeps going past it.

cards.question: How long is a woman with this kind of discharge unclean?

answers.text: All the days of her discharge

cards.text: Her bed and furniture are unclean, just like during her period. Anyone who touches them washes, bathes and is unclean until evening.

cards.question: A woman's discharge stops and she is cleansed of it. What comes next?

answers.text: She bathes and is clean that evening
She goes straight to the priest

cards.text: On the eighth day, she heads to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Same doorway the man went to, friend, so this ought to sound familiar.

cards.question: On the eighth day, the cleansed woman brings the priest two turtledoves or two young ___.
True or false: the priest sacrifices the woman's birds and makes atonement for her before the LORD.

cards.text: Then God gives the reason behind all of this. Lean in, friend, this is the big one.

cards.question: Why must the children of Israel be kept separate from their uncleanness?

answers.text: So they don't die by defiling His tabernacle
So sickness doesn't spread through the camp
So the nations around them take notice

cards.text: The law wraps up by naming every case: the man with a discharge, the emission of semen, the woman's period, any discharge, and a man who lies with an unclean woman. Not one case left out, friend, and like I said, Leviticus does NOT do small talk.
